chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man asked him about two men from the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Zimma) or from the People of War, each of whom married a woman and dowered her with wine and pigs. Then they both became Muslim. So he said: 'The marriage is valid, permissible; it is not rendered unlawful due to the wine nor due to the pigs.' I said, 'What if they became Muslim before they handed over to her the wine and the pigs?' So he said: 'When they became Muslim, it is upon him to hand over something to her from that [dower], but he should give her her dowry (sadaqah).'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْحَرْبِ: People of War (non-Muslims not under covenant)

ai.seo_question: Is a marriage valid if the couple was non-Muslim and the dowry was wine or pigs, and what happens when they convert to Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the validity of marriage for converts from Ahl al-Zimma or Polytheists is not invalidated by a dowry of wine or pork, as these items were permissible in their respective religions at the time of the contract. However, upon conversion, the husband must fulfill the obligation of providing a proper dowry, illustrating the Shia principle that prior marital bonds are preserved unless explicitly annulled, while ensuring the wife receives due rights consistent with Islamic law. This ruling underscores the flexibility of fiqh in accommodating the transition of non-Muslims into the fold of Islam without disrupting established family structures.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Talha Bin Zayd, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘A man asked himasws about two men from the Ahl Al-Zimma, or from the people of the war, each one of the two married a woman and dowered her with wine and pigs. Then they both became Muslim. So heasws said: ‘The marriage is allowed, Permissible and it is not unlawful due to the wine and pigs’. I said, ‘Supposing they both become Muslim before they hand over to her the wine and the pigs?’ So heasws said: ‘When they both became Muslim, it would be upon him that he hands over something to her and that is Mahr.
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Talhah ibn Zayd who has said the following: “

A man once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of two men of taxpayers or of those in the state of war who each married a woman and assigned a mahr (dower) in the form of wine and pigs; then they became Muslims. He (the Imam) said, ‘Marriage is permissible and lawful and it does not become unlawful because of wine and pigs.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘If they both become Muslims he must pay her something, that is, he must pay her mahr (dower).”’
